meta.title: Everything Beebo Entertainment is and offers
meta.how: Each feature has an availability label and evidence limits. Testing percentages refer to the dated checks in testing-status.json; published download versions and times come from the release feeds.

statusRules.Available: In a current download and usable today, and a person has run the main use on a real device or PC (the evidence line says what).
statusRules.Beta: In a current download or switchable today, but new, tested by automatic tests only, or with real problems found.
statusRules.In development: Being built, switched off, not in a current download, or never tried on the real equipment it needs.

features.name: Installer and updates
features.evidence: A PC updated itself from 0.1.78 to 0.1.79 while idle on Oct 5; on Oct 13 the update check on a newer test build said up to date. Not tried: updating over an older version on a second PC. Windows may show a SmartScreen warning the first time. Oct 22: a Windows test PC updated itself from 0.1.98 to 0.1.99 and the app started normally. Oct 24: Windows 0.1.102 was published (1:05 PM Eastern) and a second, older 4-core Windows PC updated itself to it from 0.1.99 (5:41 PM Eastern; hash and signature checks passed, installed in about a minute). Update Oct 27, 2026 (midday): on a second household’s PC the app updated itself twice with Nick present at times: 0.1.102 to 0.1.103 (Download update, 54 seconds) and then, fully automatic after a restart, 0.1.103 to 0.1.104 (41 seconds), each with the download hash matching the feed, a valid signature and settings kept. A start-up box “Secure media server: FAIL” still appeared after both; its cause was found and the fix is merged but not in a published build and not yet seen by a person (open). The fixed Check for updates button, the low-disk warning and uninstall are not yet tried by a person. Update Oct 28, 2026, 1:54 AM Eastern: on Oct 28, 2026 (12:16 to 12:21 AM Eastern) the app updated itself from 0.1.104 to 0.1.105 on the second household’s 4-core PC in 3 minutes 35 seconds (closed 51 seconds), the start-up box “Secure media server: FAIL” did not appear and the installer’s hash matched the website feed (an AI tester alone, Nick away). The low-disk warning, uninstall, an update while someone is watching and an update by a person are not yet tried. Windows 0.1.106 was published at 1:26 AM Eastern and its in-app update from 0.1.105 passed one test (an AI tester alone, 1:36 to 1:41 AM Eastern); its fixes have not been retested. Update Oct 28, 2026, 4:30 AM Eastern: Windows 0.1.107 was published at 3:07 AM Eastern and the app updated itself from 0.1.106 to 0.1.107 in 3 minutes 34 seconds (closed 50 seconds, Oct 28, 2026, 3:16 to 3:22 AM Eastern, an AI tester alone, Nick away); no start-up box appeared, and a copy of the downloaded installer, taken before the app removed it, matched the website feed’s hash and had a valid signature (this closes the gap that the hash could not be checked on the 0.1.106 update). The low-disk warning, uninstall, an update while someone is watching and an update by a person are not yet tried.

features.name: Library folders, scanning and matching
features.evidence: Oct 22 test-build update: The browser repair has split delivery: the server portion is reported deployed at 6:49 AM Eastern on October 22, with a further TV-browser server repair at 7:24 AM; the desktop-player portion is in unpublished Windows 0.1.100. The affected PC and combined away-route repair still need retesting. Owner-reported on October 22: on a friend’s Samsung TV built-in browser, playback away from home and Skip intro worked after repeated Reconnect clicks; ordinary poster/sidebar navigation failed without that extra step, and Up next/Next were absent at the credits. The fixed-build retry, exact TV model, browser version and served build are unconfirmed. Earlier Chromecast viewing is a separate observation with sender details unconfirmed. No new tick or broad real-world pass. The reviewed web-player Next/Full screen work is not in public downloads. Pages that suppress referrer information and a modeled cross-tab edge case remain qualified. Android version-picker results do not verify the separate desktop version-heading issue. Update Oct 26, 2026 (evening): in Chrome on a PC, converted 480p and 720p failed to start (Original played); the browser session was closed before any conversion began (open). Update Oct 27, 2026 (evening): on Windows 0.1.104 the 4-core AI tester alone (Nick away) found two new open issues: the “Resume from X?” box stays over a film that is already playing from 0:00 (3 of 3, can overwrite the saved spot; a source fix merged at about 9:32 PM Eastern is in no build), and the keyboard keys stop after Picture-in-Picture closes (3 of 3; a source fix is merged and is in no published build). Keys, captions, search and sort on a real 479-title library, seven library views and every desktop screen passed; the sound was not heard on that PC. Update Oct 28, 2026, 1:54 AM Eastern: on Windows 0.1.105 (Oct 28, 2026, 12:22 to 12:27 AM Eastern, the 4-core PC, an AI tester alone) the web player’s “Resume from…?” box held the film paused behind it on 4 of 4 films, the arrow keys worked right after Picture-in-Picture closed, and a film copied into the Movies folder appeared in about 4 seconds. On Windows 0.1.106 the desktop sidebar, TV Shows screen and Dashboard now all say 2 shows and Storage lists the shared folder once (retested by an AI tester alone). The Reconnect path was not retested.

One info page only; five shows and seasons, the missing-poster fallback and offline behaviour were not tested. Update Oct 27, 2026 (afternoon): on Windows 0.1.104 five different films showed real posters and info pages and 15 titles without artwork showed a plain “No poster” card with no broken picture (Nick and an AI tester); real TV posters showed in Chrome on a real 6-core library. The testing page now lists this as Ready (Nick confirmed; its limits are shown there): the TMDB licence for a paid product is still Nick’s decision and offline behaviour was not tested.

features.name: Direct play and on-demand conversion to 1080p, 720p and 480p
features.evidence: Oct 5 and Oct 13: the original file played; in the browser player 720p, 480p and Auto switched and kept playing from the same second. The desktop app opens films in the PC's own player; in-app playback is the phone app and the browser. Oct 24: choosing a converted 720p quality failed twice on a second household’s old 4-core PC watched from a phone on 5G through Beebo Relay (the conversion session opened and stopped; the log did not say why), while the original file played there. Update Oct 26, 2026 (evening): converted 480p, 720p and 1080p all started in under a second on the old 4-core PC through the server and the phone app; the failure is in the PC browser player (open on the web player row). Update Oct 27, 2026 (midday): on 5G through Beebo Relay, 480p chosen during a film played from the same spot after about 3 seconds (Nick saw no real pause) and the PC log showed the converter working; there is no 360p or 240p step yet. Same PC and same kind of result as Oct 26. Update Oct 27, 2026 (evening): in Chrome on Windows 0.1.104 Auto works, 720p took about 3.1 seconds with the page in front, Original 0.9 seconds and 480p 5.5 seconds (tab in the background; 4-core AI tester alone). Each quality change starts the converter at the beginning of the film once before restarting at the right place (new open issue, not fixed). The Oct 26 failure of 480p and 720p in Chrome did not repeat, but stays counted until a person confirms it.

features.name: Back up and restore settings
features.evidence: Automatic tests only.

features.name: Photos and phone backups: timeline, albums, map
features.evidence: Last PASS: Oct 24, 2026, 2:16:25 AM Eastern. One owned synthetic photo uploaded from the native S9+ selected test album. The 47,304-byte PC copy independently matched the phone source hash; the original remained. Backup was turned off and album settings restored. The native map is built in a test build only (not merged, not released, not yet seen on a phone with geotagged photos), so the earlier implementation-gap failure remains. Real map/location and pinch acceptance, restore, conflicts and broader backup behaviour are not proved. No original-file deletion was attempted. Native Android tester36 (build 86) applies only to named native actions; older passes and browser guests keep their original scope. No status or checkmark upgrade. Update Oct 26, 2026 (evening): the PC Photos screens showed the phone’s backed-up pictures (Nick: “Yes, I see it all”). Camera backup of a real photo again blanked its location data in the PC copy; that issue is open. Update Oct 27, 2026 (midday): a new photo reached the PC 3 seconds after Back up now (Android tester57, PC 0.1.104). Open: the PC copy keeps the location numbers but is missing the two direction markers, so it is not an exact copy, and the phone’s file counter said 19 files while the PC held 20. An owner setting for keeping location is written and held for review; it is not merged. Update Oct 27, 2026 (evening): on tester58 Nick and the 4-core AI tester saw the Camera backup counter go from 20 to 21 files and match the PC after Back up now, and the Keep location in photo backups switch (off by default) hold the new photo back when off and let it through when on. A byte-for-byte exact copy, videos and the first-time permission box are not shown. In Chrome the Photos page matched the PC (25 of 25 thumbnails loaded). A change that shows where on the computer the backups are saved is merged in the source code and in no published download. Update Oct 28, 2026, 7:26 AM Eastern: code, Oct 28, 2026, 7:26 AM Eastern: a small fix (the Space Saver backup notification opens Photos & Backups) is merged into the code line, in no published build; automated tests only; not tried on a device.

features.name: Space Saver: folder clean-up and encrypted private storage
features.evidence: Last PASS Oct 24, 2026, 2:16:25 AM Eastern (carried without rerun). A real Galaxy S9+ running native Android tester36 (build 86) uploaded one newly created synthetic photo from its selected test album. The PC copy matched all 47,304 bytes and the original file hash. The phone showed Up to date; its original remained and backup was turned off afterward. This is backup integrity only. Full album backfill, freeing space, deletion, encrypted-storage acceptance, restore, conflicts, disk-full and NAS behaviour remain untested. Development server 0.1.99; installed Windows application never launched. Final ledgers reconciled, no new whole-feature checkmark. Update Oct 26, 2026 (evening): the Scan compared correctly and deleted nothing; “Back up now” for a new photo failed twice on the same Wi-Fi (cause not proven; open). Update Oct 27, 2026 (midday): the Oct 26 failure of “Back up now” on a new photo did not repeat on Android tester57 with the PC on 0.1.104 (the photo reached the PC in 3 seconds). New open issue: the PC copy is not byte-identical to the original (two location direction markers are missing). Freeing space and deleting were not tried. Update Oct 27, 2026 (evening): the Converted Videos screen (where Space Saver appears) was read on Windows 0.1.104: 2 conversions, sizes shown, nothing pressed or deleted.

faq.a: Beebo is a free, local-first media server with apps. It runs on your own Windows computer, holds the movies, shows, music, photos, audiobooks, podcasts and radio that you already own, and streams them to your phone, tablet, TV, car or any web browser. Beebo includes no movies or shows; you bring your own files.

The Windows server and the apps are free to use at home. Optional extras such as Beebo Relay (Beta) and BeeboVPN (In development) are listed with their status, and their terms are not final. Prices are listed on one page only, the pricing page, and Relay is not available to buy yet.
No. Beebo's own code is closed source and all rights are reserved. It does use third-party open-source components, and the apps include a notices screen that lists them.

faq.q: Does my video go through Beebo's servers?
faq.a: Whenever possible, video goes straight from your computer to the viewer. Beebo's servers carry only small text such as sign-in and connection set-up. If a direct connection cannot be made, the optional Beebo Relay (Beta) can carry the video; it is end-to-end encrypted and the relay cannot see it.

The server runs on Windows 10 and 11 and is Available. You watch with the Android test app, in any web browser, or by casting to a Chromecast. Linux and Docker or NAS are Beta. Fire TV, Roku, LG, Samsung, Xbox, macOS and the native iPhone, iPad and Apple TV apps are In development and have not been tested on real hardware.
No. The Android app is a test download from this website that you install yourself. The Google Play version is in development and has not been submitted.

Many things. The full list on this page says exactly which features are Available, Beta, In development or Planned, what was tested on real devices and when, and what nobody has tested yet. Examples: TV apps on real TVs, a real tuner, a real Mac, a real Linux desktop, and most of Beebo Auto beyond one real car check.

faq.q: How is the completion percentage worked out?
faq.a: It is a share-of-list count, not a promise and not an audit. For example, the share of listed features whose label is Available. The rules and the data file are on this page, and the numbers are calculated from that file by a script.

faq.q: What does Beebo keep about me?
faq.a: Your files stay on your own computer. Beebo keeps the amount of data used per account and basic connection records, including IP addresses, for 7 days for abuse checks. Nothing is sold.

faq.q: Do you test on real devices?
faq.a: Yes, on our own devices: a Galaxy S24 Ultra, a Galaxy S9+, a Chromecast TV, Windows PCs and one real car on one drive. These are our own checks, not a broad beta. Every line says what was tried and what was not.
